= CHERIoT memory subsystem: checker 1 (tag path) microarchitecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures
:fpv: ../opentitan/hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv

This is the microarchitecture of FPV (formal property verification) checker 1 of the CHERIoT memory
subsystem (`cheriot_mem_sys`): the testbench that checks the tag path, from the core's port
`cored_tl_d` to the RMW (read-modify-write) filter's downstream port. It implements every check and
cover that the xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#checker1[testplan] lists for
checker 1, and it shows, testpoint by testpoint, how each check is performed: when it looks, what it
expects, what testbench state it reads, a passing trace, and the bug it catches. The checker's
boundary, environment and contracts are set in the xref:cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#tag_path[TB
architecture]; the TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) rules on its ports come from the shared
TL-UL ABVIP (assertion-based verification IP;
xref:../../tlul_abvip/tb_arch/tlul_abvip_uarch.adoc[ABVIP microarchitecture]). The checker is bound
into the design and holds its rules on what its neighbours send, assumed in formal and checked in
simulation, so it is also meant to be bound into simulation (simulation).

== Overview

=== In one page

*Rule:* checker 1 is a formal testbench: it proves that the tag path of `cheriot_mem_sys` does what
the spec says, for every input sequence its environment allows, not for a sample of them.

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Question |Answer

|What is checked? |The tag path, as real RTL: the core's tag filter with its WTRC, the 2:1 tag
arbiter, the tag clear squash and the RMW filter, from the core's port `cored_tl_d` to the RMW
filter's port towards the meta SRAM (<<What checker 1 checks>>)
|What does the testbench play? |The blocks around it: the core, `xbar_main`, the engine's tag
filter and the tag access checker. Each is a TL-UL ABVIP that sends only legal traffic, plus a few
rules this design needs (<<Environment>>)
|How is it checked? |The testbench works out from the spec what each block must send: a model of the
tag filter, a model of the RMW filter, a tracker, and functions for the arbiter. Properties compare
each prediction with what the RTL sends. Covers show that each case can happen, so no check passes
without being exercised
|What exactly? |The testplan's 21 testpoints for checker 1, in five groups: tag filter, WTRC,
arbiter, RMW filter, and alerts with contracts (<<What checker 1 checks>>)
|How do I read one? |Every testpoint has the same walkthrough: its rule in plain words, its checks,
its covers, a passing trace and the bugs it catches; then a link to its code
(<<How to read a walkthrough>>)
|===

'''

=== What checker 1 checks

*Rule:* checker 1 holds the real tag path, from `cored_tl_d` to the RMW filter's downstream port,
and implements every check and cover the testplan lists for it, and nothing else.

The tag path, block by block ([DA] block table): the core's tag filter passes each core request to
`xbar_main` and, when the request needs a tag, sends a tag request on its meta port. The 2:1 tag
arbiter merges those tag requests with the engine's: the TBRE (background revocation engine), which
clears tags and has a tag filter of its own. The tag clear squash passes the core's tag requests on
unchanged, and turns an engine's tag clear that a core write overtook into a read. The RMW filter
turns each tag access into whole-word reads and writes of the meta SRAM, the memory that holds the
tags. The other terms are in <<How to read a walkthrough>>.

=== How the testbench is built

*Rule:* checker 1 lives in the one FPV environment of `cheriot_mem_sys` ([TB] One environment, one
task per checker): the FPV top, `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env`, holds `cheriot_mem_sys` with every input
free, and one shared module is bound into the design, the one checker, which holds `tpchk_checker`:
every check of checker 1 and every rule on what its neighbours send. Each rule is written with the
`ENV_RULE` macro: an assumption in a formal build, an assertion in a simulation. Each layer is a
module or a banner section of its own and talks to the others through named signals; only the wiring
knows RTL names (formal-verification skill, TB architecture). Checker 1 has three Jasper tasks:
`task_TagPath_Main`, with every check that can share one setup, and two for checks that cannot
(<<Environment>>). Checker 1's own FPV top, `tpchk_env`, and its assumption module were
retired.

.Checker 1's testbench: the FPV top holds the design; the checker, with its rules, is bound in

|`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env` |The FPV top, shared. Every input of `cheriot_mem_sys` is an input of

|rules |A section of `tpchk_checker` that keeps those inputs legal: the TL-UL ABVIPs on the four
ports the testbench plays, and the rules on top of them. The checker is bound inside
`cheriot_mem_sys`, so the rules also reach the two ports inside the design whose other end is a
blackbox: arbiter input 1 and the RMW filter downstream. In a simulation the same rules are checked

|events |inside the checker: the four handshake events of each port (<<Port events>>), read by

|predictions |inside the checker: what the models and the tracker expect the RTL to send, read by

=== How to read a walkthrough

*Rule:* each testpoint has one walkthrough, with the same parts in the same order
(formal-verification skill, TB architecture, Check walkthroughs). The first four parts explain the
testpoint; the covers, collapsed, and the code link are its bookkeeping.

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Holds

|Implements |the testpoint, its requirements, its rule in plain words, and its formula from the
testplan
|Check table |one row per check: when it looks (its trigger), what it expects, and its run
|Passing trace |a waveform of one legal trace with the cycles where each check looks, then a cycle
table
|Bug it catches |one row per line of the testpoint's *Never*: what a faulty design would do, and
the check that fails
|Covers |collapsed: the testplan's covers for the testpoint, and what each one reaches
|Code |a link to the testpoint's banner section in the checker file: the property behind each
check, the testbench state it reads, and the properties that reach each cover
|===

Terms used in every walkthrough:

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning

|presented |valid is high: `a_valid` for a request, `d_valid` for an answer
|taken, accepted |valid and ready are both high: the transfer happens ([TLUL])
|first cycle |the first cycle a core request is presented; it stays presented until accepted (assumption A1)
|entry |the tag filter model's record of one core request, from its first cycle until its answer is
taken
|head |the oldest entry that was accepted: its answer is the one due next on `cored_tl_d`
|owed |a WTRC tag write the meta port must take before anything else
|`trk` |the one core request the tracker follows
|xbar request |the request the tag filter forwards to `xbar_main` on `cored_tl_h`, the port the
spec calls the host port ([ToO] Theory of Operation). The testbench names this port's events after
the block at the other end, because in TL-UL "host" is the role of whoever sends requests
|xbar answer |`xbar_main`{empty}'s answer to the xbar request, on `cored_tl_h`; the testplan calls it the
host answer, and its `d_error` is the testplan's `HostErr`
|W0, W1 |the two 32-bit words of a 64-bit capability: W0 at the lower address (bit 2 is 0), W1 four
bytes above it
|hinted |a core read with its tag sideband set: the core asks for the tag too, as it does for both
words of a capability load ([CIBEX], [LSU] `data_tag_o`)
|meta SRAM, meta word, meta port |the memory that holds one tag bit per capability, a 32-bit word of
it, and the tag filter's port that asks for it (the meta request and the meta answer)
|engine |the TBRE (background revocation engine), which clears tags; it has a tag filter of its own,
blackboxed here, on arbiter input 1
|tag clear squash |the logic between the 2:1 tag arbiter and the RMW filter that turns an engine's tag
clear, overtaken by a core write, into a read ([DA] block table)
|WTRC |the write-to-read-and-compare filter in the tag filter: a capability store to the NVM
(non-volatile memory) is not written but read and compared, and the tag is set only if both words
match
|CHERIoT mode, ePMP mode |`cheriot_ena_i` is exactly `MuBi4True`: tags are looked up and written.
Any other value: ePMP mode (enhanced physical memory protection, the RISC-V scheme used without
CHERIoT), with no tag lookups. `MuBi4True` is a multi-bit boolean: one flipped bit cannot turn the
mode on ([DA] modes; [ToO] Block Diagram)
|bitmap, bitmap window |the revocation bitmap at the base of the meta SRAM ([ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map), and `revbm_tl_d`, the window through which `xbar_main` reaches it
|the seam |`0x1002_0000`, where the main SRAM meets the second SRAM inside one tagged region; the
tags on both sides sit in consecutive meta words (testplan, Definitions)
|`clc`, `csc`, `lw`, `sw`, `sb` |the core's instructions: capability load and store (two words each), load and store word, store byte ([ISA])
|DV reading |what DV (design verification) reads the spec to imply, where the spec does not state
it
|===

* Inside a walkthrough, a bare A1 or C1 is that testpoint's own check or cover. An assumption, a
  contract or another testpoint's check always says so: assumption A2, contract C6, `tf_flow` A1.
* A property's label says what it guarantees, `<kind>_<Feature>_<Name>`, with no check ID:
  `assert_TfLookup_NoUnneededLookup` is check A2 of `tf_lookup`, `cover_TfLookup_StoreWord` its
  cover C4. The two lines above each property give its requirements and its testplan check, and the
  check map (check map) links every check to its label. Labels were renamed (old to new:
  `out/label_rename/rename_map.tsv`).
* Every check is in `task_TagPath_Main` unless its row says otherwise. The Task column of a check
  table gives the part of the task's name after `task_TagPath_`: `Main`, `TagsRspTaken` or
  `EveryReqAnswered` (<<Environment>>; [TP] Run variants; [TB] Proof order). A core that breaks its
  access order is out of scope ([TP] Not covered by this testplan), so no task drops assumptions A3
  and A4.

== Testbench microarchitecture

=== Definitions in the testbench

*Rule:* every formula of the testplan's Definitions is one function in `tpchk_pkg`, computed from
the spec's numbers, never from the RTL's. The function for each formula is in the Details block
below.

The table base addresses are computed from the address map, as [ToO] lays it out: the bitmap
takes `(0x1003_0000 - 0x1000_0000) / 256 * 4 = 0xC00` bytes, so the NVM tags start at `0x1100_0C00`,
and the NVM tags take `0x20_0000 / 256 * 4 = 0x8000` bytes, so the main SRAM tags start at
`0x1100_8C00`. The worked numbers below were computed with the same formulas in a script.

[cols="2,2,1",options="header"]
|===
|Address |`TagWord` |`TagBit`

|`0x1000_1238`, `0x1000_123C` (W0 and W1 of one capability) |`0x1100_8C48` |7
|`0x1000_1240` |`0x1100_8C48` |8
|`0x1001_FFF8`, `0x1002_0000` (the seam) |`0x1100_93FC`, `0x1100_9400` |31, 0
|`0x3000_0400` |`0x1100_0C10` |0
|`0x301F_FFF8`, the last NVM capability |`0x1100_8BFC` |31
|===

'''

=== Bind

*Rule:* the shared bind and the FPV top's port list are the only places with RTL names, so a
renamed net changes them and nothing else. `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker_bind` binds the one
checker, in formal and in simulation; the rules use the checker's own ports, so a simulation gets
them with the same bind (simulation).

* No run define: one build holds every check and every rule, and each Jasper task copies its own
  (task table in <<Environment>>).
* Each bind sits inside a `default_nettype none` directive, so a misspelt net
  name is an error, not a new floating wire that Verilator only warns about (`IMPLICIT`). With it,
  the FPV top and both binds elaborate with Verilator 5.048 on the RTL files of
  `cheriot_mem_sys`, with and without `FPV_ON`, with no error and no warning from the testbench
  files: every net name in the Details block below exists.

'''

=== Port events

*Rule:* each port's handshake is decoded once, in the checker's Port events section, into four
events the models and the properties use by name ([TLUL] Signals: "a beat passes in a cycle where valid and ready are both
high"). The environment uses the events its ABVIPs export instead.

[cols="1,3,4",options="header"]
|===
|Event |Formula |Meaning

|`req_vld` |`a_valid` |a request is presented
|`req_fire` |`a_valid && a_ready` |the request is taken
|`rsp_vld` |`d_valid` |an answer is presented
|`rsp_fire` |`d_valid && d_ready` |the answer is taken
|===

Seven ports get events: `cored_tl_d` (`core`), `cored_tl_h` (`xbar`), arbiter inputs 0 and 1
(`m[0]`, `m[1]`), the arbiter output (`arb`), the RMW filter upstream (`rmw`) and downstream
(`tags`). The arbiter output's events use the RMW filter's `a_ready` and D channel, which the tag
clear squash passes through unchanged.

'''

=== Environment

*Rule:* every rule of checker 1 on what its neighbours send sits in the rules section of
`tpchk_checker`: a TL-UL ABVIP on each of the four ports the testbench plays, and the rules on top
of the ABVIPs, each written with `ENV_RULE`, an assumption in formal and an assertion in simulation.
Each rule names its row of the design architecture's Assumptions, or its contract. The ABVIP holds only
TL-UL's own rules; every restriction of this design is a rule of its own on top
(formal-verification skill, TB architecture, Reuse).

Each ABVIP assumes the TL-UL rules of the end it plays, so the tool drives only legal traffic, and
asserts the rules of the design's end.

[cols="2,3,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Instance |Port |Plays |Its one restriction beyond TL-UL

|`u_abvip_core` |`cored_tl_d` |the core (host) |at most two requests outstanding: a third only in
the cycle an answer is taken (assumption A2)
|`u_abvip_xbar` |`cored_tl_h` |`xbar_main` (device) |none
|`u_abvip_m1` |arbiter input 1 |the engine's tag filter (host) |its waiting requests differ in the
low 7 bits of `a_source` (assumption A9)
|`u_abvip_tags` |RMW filter downstream |the tag access checker (device) |none
|===

* *Why only 7 bits on arbiter input 1:* the arbiter adds the input number at the bottom of
  `a_source`, so the top bit of an input's `a_source` is lost, as [TLUL] allows. The ABVIP
  therefore matches answers on the low 7 bits.
* *The two links between real blocks,* arbiter input 0 and the RMW filter upstream, have no ABVIP
  here: the testbench plays neither end. Their `CheckBoth` ABVIPs sit in the checker, since they
  assume nothing. The checker's own properties also check hold, ready and flow
  there: `contracts` checks A7 and A2, `rmw_single_op` A4, `tf_flow` A1 and `arb_flow` A3.
* Integrity is free on every port: a broken integrity is legal stimulus (`REQ_TAG_08` needs it).

The rules on top of the ABVIPs:

[cols="2,6,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Assumption |Rule |Basis |Tasks

|A1 |a core request and its tag stay unchanged until accepted |[LSU] `data_req_o`; gap, raised with the designers |all
|A3 |a capability load is a hinted full-word read of W0, then, as the next request, a hinted read of
W0 + 4; a hinted read of a W1 address comes only as that W1 |[CIBEX] two consecutive
transactions; [LSU] `data_tag_o`; answered by the designers |all
|A4 |a capability store to the NVM is two full words, W0 then W1, and nothing else is presented
until W1 is answered |[ToO] WTRC |all
|A5 |a `PutPartialData` carries tag 0 |[ISA] §7.7 |all
|A6 |`cheriot_ena_i` keeps its value from reset |[ToO]; answered by the designers |all
|A7 |`xbar_main` answers in request order |[LSU] Protocol; answered by the designers |all
|A14 |`xbar_main` answers a cycle or more after it takes the request |gap: a finding raised with the designers |all
|A15 |`xbar_main` holds an answer, unchanged, until it is taken |gap: a finding raised with the designers |all
|A9 |the core's `a_source` bits 7:5 are 0: one bit is left free for the 2:1 tag arbiter, two for
the 4:1 arbiter |[TLUL] Source ID growth |all
|contract C3a |the engine's tag filter holds its meta request, tag and bit select until accepted
|proven in checker 3 |all
|contract C11 |the engine's tag filter addresses whole meta words |proven in checker 3 |all
|contract C10 |the tag access checker answers a cycle or more after it takes the request, in
request order, and holds each answer unchanged until it is taken |proven in checker 2, assuming
[DA] A16 |all
|assumption A10, premise P5 |the core takes every answer, at some point |the condition of
`REQ_TF_15b` |EveryReqAnswered
|A10 |`xbar_main` accepts every request, and answers while one is outstanding, at some point |the
condition of `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b` (DV reading) |EveryReqAnswered
|contract C1 |the tag access checker accepts every request, and answers while one is outstanding,
at some point |proven in checker 2 |EveryReqAnswered
|contract C3b |the engine's tag filter takes each meta answer in the cycle it is offered |proven in
checker 3 |TagsRspTaken, EveryReqAnswered
|===

[cols="2,1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Task |Runs |What it checks, under which rules

|`task_TagPath_Main` |V1 |every safety check, the alert checks (they need no fairness) and every
cover; every rule except contracts C3b, C1, premise P5 and assumption A10
|`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` |liveness A |adds contract C3b; checks `contracts` A4, which is
contract C4: the RMW filter takes every answer offered downstream. It assumes no other contract:
checker 2 proves contract C1 assuming contract C4 ([TB] Proof order, stage 2)
|`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered` |liveness B |adds contracts C3b and C1, premise P5 and assumption
A10; checks `tf_flow` A3 and A4, `arb_flow` A3, `rmw_single_op` A4 and `contracts` A2 (contract
C2). Runs once checker 2 has proven contract C1 ([TB] Proof order, stage 4)
|===

* *Why three tasks:* contract C3b is a safety rule, the engine's tag filter taking each meta answer
  in the cycle it is offered. In the main task it would void every check on an engine answer that
  waits. The two liveness tasks cannot be one: `task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered` assumes the access
  checker contract (C1), which checker 2 proves assuming the contract that the RMW filter takes
  every answer (C4), so that contract must be proven without C1 ([TB] Proof order).
  There is no task for a core that breaks its access order: that is out of scope ([TP] Not covered
  by this testplan).
* *Free variable:* `pick`, the core request the tracker follows, sits in the checker. It is undriven
  under `FPV_ON`, so the tool picks it in every cycle, and 1 in simulation (simulation). It
  needs no rule, so the environment has none for it. The check script puts a cut point on it, which
  makes it free.
* The arbiter checks need no free variable: each runs on both inputs, in a loop, so a simulation
  checks both too.
* The RTL contains its own assumption, `ASSUME(CoredReqHeld_M, ...)` (`cheriot_mem_sys.sv` L787).
  Assumption A1 implies it, but in FPV it would be a second constraint outside the checker's rules.
  The check script leaves it out of every checker 1 task (jasper setup).

*Code:* the `rules:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

=== Tag filter model

*Rule:* the tag filter model keeps every core request in order, from its first cycle on
`cored_tl_d` until its answer is taken, joins to it its xbar answer and its meta answer as they
arrive, and gives the answer the spec requires for the oldest one ([ToO] Tag Filter, WTRC).

What it models: the tag filter and its WTRC, the design under test; not the core. The core is
played by `u_abvip_core` and the core's rules, assumptions A1-A5 and A9 (<<Environment>>). The model drives no port:
it observes the tag filter's ports and predicts what the tag filter must send; the properties
compare each prediction with what the RTL sends.

'''

==== Observed, modeled, checked

*Rule:* the model observes the seven events on the tag filter's ports, keeps what the spec needs
from them, and predicts what the tag filter must send on each of its outputs, (4) to (7); one group
of properties per output compares the prediction with what the RTL sends ([ToO] Tag Filter, WTRC).

nothing to check

`Lookup(r)`, in its first cycle, of word `TagWord(a)` and bit `TagBit(a)`, carrying a write's tag

A1

  (for example `head_tag`, `presented_entry.xbar_req_fired`).
* The model observes the outputs (4) to (7) too: what the tag filter has already done decides

'''

==== One request, step by step

*Rule:* each event lands in the entry of the request it belongs to, whatever the order the events
come in; the checks look in the cycle the RTL sends an output.

A capability load's W0, a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_1238` whose stored tag is 1, as in the figure:

[cols="2,7,5,5,6",options="header"]
|===
|Step |Event |Sent by |The model records |Checked here

|1 |W0 presented on `cored_tl_d` |testbench: `u_abvip_core` |a new entry: `KindLoadW0`, `lookup`
|`tf_forward` A1 and `tf_lookup` A1 start: steps 2 and 3 are due in this cycle
|2 |W0 forwarded on `cored_tl_h` |RTL: the tag filter |`xbar_req_fired` |`tf_forward` A1, A2
|3 |the lookup of `0x1100_8C48`, bit 7, on the meta port |RTL: the tag filter |`meta_req_fired`
|`tf_lookup` A1, A2; `tf_meta_request` A1-A3
|4 |W0 accepted on `cored_tl_d` (`a_ready`) |RTL: the tag filter |`core_req_fired` |`tf_forward` A5
|5 |the xbar answer, `AccessAckData` |testbench: `u_abvip_xbar` |`xbar_rsp_fired`, `xbar_rsp_err` 0 |an
input
|6 |the meta answer, tag 1 |RTL: the arbiter and the RMW filter; the word they read comes from
`u_abvip_tags` |`meta_rsp_vld_seen`, `meta_rsp_tag` 1 |`tf_flow` A1: the tag filter takes it at once
|7 |the answer on `cored_tl_d`, tag 1 |RTL: the tag filter |nothing new: it predicts tag 1,
`d_error` 0, the xbar answer's fields |`tf_forward` A3, A4; `tf_sticky_tag` A1; `tf_errors` A1,
A2; `tf_flow` A2
|8 |the answer taken (`d_ready`) |testbench: `u_abvip_core` |the entry leaves |-
|===

* Steps 1 to 4 may happen in one cycle, and steps 5 and 6 in either order ([ToO] Timing). The
  entry is what lets them meet: whatever the order, each part lands in the entry of its request.
* Every arrow in the figure is a port of the design. The model sees all of them and drives none.

'''

==== The entry

*Rule:* one entry per core request, from its first cycle on `cored_tl_d` until its answer is taken;
Assumption A2 keeps two between cycles, and a third only in the cycle an answer frees a place.

Why a model of every request rather than one tracked request: the tag the spec requires for an
answer depends on the answers before it (the capture), and the WTRC's tag write depends on both
words of a capability store. Both need the order of all requests.

An entry (type `entry_t`) holds two sorts of field. The first sort says what the request is: it is
set in the request's first cycle and never changes. The second sort says how far the request has
got: each field is set by one event, with what that event carried, so the checks ask "has it
happened yet?" and never count cycles. `kind` is the request's type (`req_kind`: another read,
W0 or W1 of a capability load, a write, a capability store to the NVM).

[cols="2,5,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Entry field |Holds |Filled when |Sent by

4+|*What the request is: set in its first cycle, never changed*
|`kind`, `lookup`, `w1`, `addr`, `src` |the request's kind (`req_kind`), `Lookup(r)`, address bit 2,
address, `a_source` |its first cycle on `cored_tl_d` |testbench: `u_abvip_core`
|`out_of_seq`, `fault`, `full_in_seq` |out of the capability store sequence; a faulty capability
store word; a full-word `PutFullData` in sequence |its first cycle, judged against the WTRC
sequence |the model (<<WTRC sequence>>)
|`data`, `data_intg` |the data and data integrity it writes: `Data(w)`, `DataIntg(w)` |its first
cycle |testbench: `u_abvip_core`
4+|*How far it has got: set as each event happens*
|`core_req_fired` |accepted on `cored_tl_d` |`a_ready` with it |RTL: the tag filter
|`xbar_req_fired` |its xbar request taken on `cored_tl_h` |the tag filter's request taken |RTL: the tag
filter
|`xbar_rsp_fired`, `xbar_rsp_err`, `xbar_rsp_intg_bad` |its xbar answer taken, with `d_error`, with a bad
response integrity |the xbar answer |testbench: `u_abvip_xbar`
|`match` |a capability store word: `Match(w)` against its NVM answer |its xbar answer |the model,
from the xbar answer
|`tag_wr`, `tag_wr_maybe` |W1: its tag write is owed or sent; may be sent (after a broken sequence) |W1's NVM answer |the model, from both words' answers
|`meta_req_fired` |its lookup or tag write taken on the meta port |the tag filter's meta request taken
|RTL: the tag filter
|`meta_rsp_vld_seen`, `meta_rsp_err`, `meta_rsp_tag` |its meta answer arrived, with `d_error` and its tag |the
meta answer |RTL: the arbiter and the RMW filter
|===

'''

==== How the parts are joined

*Rule:* each answer belongs to the oldest entry still waiting for that kind of answer; the answer
due on `cored_tl_d` is always the oldest accepted entry's.

[cols="2,4,5",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Belongs to |Why that is safe

|xbar answer |the oldest entry whose xbar request was taken and whose xbar answer was not |assumption A7:
`xbar_main` answers in request order; each core request makes exactly one xbar request
(`tf_forward` A2, A5), in core order
|meta answer |the oldest entry whose lookup or tag write was taken and whose meta answer has not
arrived |the RMW filter does one operation at a time (`REQ_RMW_10`) and the arbiter returns each
answer to the input that asked (`REQ_ARB_05`); both are checked in this checker
|answer on `cored_tl_d` |the head: the oldest accepted entry |contract C6, asserted by the
checker (contracts A6): the tag filter answers in request order
|===

* A part presented in this cycle counts as arrived: the tag filter may pass it through in the same
  cycle ([ToO] Timing). A xbar answer the tag filter has not taken yet is read live from
  `cored_tl_h`.
* A meta answer is always taken when it is offered (`tf_flow` A1), so it arrives when it is
  presented.

A capability load (`clc`) of `0x1000_1238`, with stored tag 1, through the model:

[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |On the ports |Entries and capture after the cycle

|1 |W0: a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_1238` presented and taken on `cored_tl_d`; its xbar request and
its meta request (`0x1100_8C48`, bit 7) both taken |entry 0: `KindLoadW0`, `lookup`, `xbar_req_fired`,
`meta_req_fired`, `core_req_fired`
|2 |W1: a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_123C` presented and taken; its xbar request taken; no meta
request |entry 1: `KindLoadW1`, `xbar_req_fired`, `core_req_fired`
|3 |the xbar answer to W0 and the meta answer, tag 1, both arrive; the answer to W0 is presented,
tag 1, and taken |entry 0 leaves; entry 1 moves up; capture: `CaptureHeld`, tag 1
|4 |the xbar answer to W1 arrives; the answer to W1 is presented, tag 1 (the capture), and taken
|entry 0 leaves; capture: `CaptureNone`
|===

'''

==== WTRC sequence

*Rule:* the model follows the capability store sequence as [ToO] WTRC describes it, to tell an
in-sequence request from an out-of-sequence one and to know when W1's tag write is owed.

In plain words: the core stores a 64-bit capability as two 32-bit words, W0 then W1. The NVM
cannot be written, so the WTRC reads each word back from the NVM and compares it with what the
core sent. Only when both words match does it write the capability's tag. The model follows the
same steps, so it knows two things: when W1's tag write is owed, and which request comes out of
sequence (a fault, which must raise the alert). The figure shows one store that succeeds; each
note on the left is the model's stage after that event, and what counts as a fault there.

[cols="1,7,3",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens |The model after it

|1 |The core sends W0: a `PutFullData` of `0x3000_0400` with tag 1. The tag filter takes it.
|`CapW0`: a capability is open
|2 |The WTRC turns W0 into a `Get` of the same word: it reads the NVM instead of writing it. No
lookup. |-
|3 |The core sends W1, `0x3000_0404`. The tag filter takes it. |`CapW1`
|4 |W1 becomes a `Get` too. |-
|5 |The NVM answers W0: the same data and data integrity. |`Match(W0)` = 1, kept
|6 |The WTRC answers W0 itself: `AccessAck`, no `d_error`. |-
|7 |The NVM answers W1: it matches too. |the tag write is owed
|8 |The meta port takes the tag write: tag 1 to bit 0 of meta word `0x1100_0C10`. |`CapTagWr`
|9 |The tag write's answer arrives. |-
|10 |W1 is answered with the tag write's result. |`CapIdle`: closed
|===

If either word differs from the NVM, step 8 never happens: W1 is answered with `d_error`, and the
model goes from `CapW1` straight back to `CapIdle`. The table below lists every stage, what is out
of sequence there, and every way out. The ways marked "out of scope" need a core that breaks its
access order, which no task allows ([TP] Not covered by this testplan); the model keeps them, so it
stays defined for every input.

[cols="2,2,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Stage |Model name |Out of sequence here (a fault) |Leaves when

|No capability open |`CapIdle` |a W1 |a W0 is accepted: `CapW0`
|W0 taken |`CapW0` |anything but the W1 of the same capability |its W1 is accepted: `CapW1`. Out
of scope: another W0 is accepted and opens a new capability: `CapW0`
|W1 taken |`CapW1` |any request |the tag write is taken: `CapTagWr`; W1's answer is taken without
a tag write: `CapIdle`. Out of scope: a W0 is accepted: `CapW0`
|Tag write sent |`CapTagWr` |a W1, or a W0 |W1's answer is taken: `CapIdle`. Out of scope: a W0
is accepted: `CapW0`
|===

* "A W0 taken always opens a capability, and W1's answer closes it" (testplan, WTRC sequence).
  Assumption A4 allows a W0 only when no capability is open, or in the cycle W1 is answered, which
  the model judges against `CapIdle`; so the ways marked out of scope are never taken.
* A request is judged in its first cycle. In the cycle W1's answer is taken, it is judged against
  `CapIdle`: "the next W0 may be taken in the cycle W1 is answered".
* `Match(W0)` is kept when W0's NVM answer arrives. When W1's NVM answer arrives and both words
  matched with no fault, the tag write is owed until the meta port takes it.
* *Broken sequence:* when another request comes out of sequence while a capability is open, the
  spec does not say whether the open capability may still set its tag. The model then neither
  requires nor forbids its tag write (`tag_wr_maybe`), and does not check W1's `d_error`; the faulty
  request itself is still checked, and the alert. No task reaches it: such a core is out of scope.

'''

==== Capture of the tag

*Rule:* the tag of a capability load's W0 answer is captured and returned again with the W1 answer,
then cleared ([ToO] Tag Filter); the model follows it per answer taken.

In plain words: a capability is 64 bits and one tag bit, but the core reads it as two 32-bit
answers, W0 then W1. Only W0 asks the meta SRAM for the tag. The tag filter remembers ("captures")
that tag, sends it again with W1's answer, then forgets it. The model does the same, so it knows
which tag each answer must carry. The figure follows the capability load of `0x1000_1238`, whose
stored tag is 1, cycle by cycle, as in <<How the parts are joined>>.

[cols="1,7,3",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens |Capture

|1 |W0, a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_1238`, is taken. Its lookup goes to meta word `0x1100_8C48`,
bit 7. |empty (`CaptureNone`)
|2 |W1, `0x1000_123C`, is taken. W1 has no lookup. |empty
|3 |The meta answer brings tag 1. W0's answer goes to the core with that tag, and the model
captures it. |empty; 1 from the next cycle
|4 |W1's answer goes to the core with the captured tag, 1. |1 (`CaptureHeld`); cleared after
this cycle
|5 |Nothing captured, as after reset: a W1 answer now would carry tag 0. |empty (`CaptureNone`)
|===

The table below lists every state, with the cases the figure does not show: a write or a plain
read answered between W0 and W1.

[cols="4,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Model name |The W1 answer's tag must be

|nothing captured: after reset, or after a W1 answer |`CaptureNone` |0 (`REQ_TF_10`)
|W0's tag captured; a write answered between W0 and W1 keeps it |`CaptureHeld` |the captured tag
(`REQ_TF_09`, `REQ_TF_11b`)
|a plain read was answered between W0 and W1: the spec is open (testplan, `tf_sticky_tag`). The
next W0 answer captures again; a W1 answer clears it |`CaptureUnknown` |not checked
|===

The capture is taken even when W0's answer has `d_error` (testplan case `tf_sticky_tag` C8); only
the W0 answer's own tag goes unchecked then.

'''

==== Fault causes

*Rule:* the model flags each of [ToO] Error Handling's fault causes in the cycle it occurs, and
remembers that one occurred since reset; the alert checks compare the WTRC's fault input with these.

[cols="4,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Cause ([ToO] Error Handling) |When the model sees it |Output

|a capability store word out of sequence, partial, or with a bad command or data integrity |its
first cycle |`word_cause_now`
|a bad response integrity on a capability store word's NVM answer |the NVM answer arrives
|`word_cause_now`
|any other request out of sequence |its first cycle |`out_of_seq_cause_now`
|any of these, since reset |- |`cause_seen`
|===

'''

=== Tracker

*Rule:* the tracker follows one core request, picked by the free variable `pick` in its first
cycle, keeps its xbar answer when the tag filter takes it, and gives it back when that request's
answer is due (formal-verification skill, Symbolic tracking).

In plain words: to check every field of an answer, the testbench must remember the xbar answer it
came from. Keeping it for every request would cost about 130 flops. Instead the tool picks one
request, and the tracker keeps only that request's xbar answer and compares it with the answer the
core gets. The tool may pick any request, so every request is checked. The figure follows the
capability load of `0x1000_1238` of <<How the parts are joined>>, cycle by cycle, with W1 picked:
W1's messages are in magenta, and the left column says what the tracker does at each one.

[cols="1,5,6,4",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |On the ports |The tracker |Why

|1 |W0, a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_1238`, arrives and is forwarded |`pick` is 0: it stays free
(`TrkIdle`) |the tool sets `pick` in every cycle, so any request can be the followed one
|2 |W1, a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_123C`, arrives and is forwarded |`pick` is 1: it follows W1
(`TrkOn`) and notes W1's place: 2nd in line (entry 1), behind W0 |answers come back in request
order, so W1's comes after W0's
|3 |W0's xbar answer and its meta answer (tag 1, <<Capture of the tag>>) arrive; W0's answer goes
to the core and is taken |W0 leaves: W1 moves up to 1st in line (entry 0) |the next answer to the
core is W1's
|4 |W1's xbar answer arrives; W1's answer goes to the core in the same cycle and is taken |reads
W1's xbar answer live on `cored_tl_h`; `tf_forward` A3 checks that W1's answer carries its
opcode, size, source, data and integrity. W1's answer taken: it is free again (`TrkIdle`) |the tag
filter may pass a xbar answer through in the cycle it arrives ([ToO] Timing)
|===

* If the tag filter takes W1's xbar answer before W1's turn, the tracker keeps a copy (66 bits) and
  checks W1's answer against the copy.
* `tf_errors` A3 uses the same xbar answer: when a meta error is merged into the answer, the
  answer's integrity must stay valid or broken as the xbar answer's was.
* Coverage: the Jasper setup creates a precondition cover for every assert (related covers,
  formal-verification skill, jasper-tcl.md). Those of `tf_forward` A3 and `tf_errors` A3 need the
  tracked request at the head with its answer presented, so they reach `TrkOn`; the `tf_errors`
  Row4 covers need its answer taken, so they reach the end. The tracker does not read the mode, so
  one mode is enough. No cover of its own is added: every property names a testplan check
  (check map).
* In simulation `pick` is 1: the tracker follows the next core request whenever it is free, so
  over a test it follows many requests, one after another (simulation).

'''

=== RMW model

*Rule:* the RMW model follows the RMW filter's one operation, from its acceptance upstream to its
answer taken, and says which downstream request may come next and what the answer must be ([ToO]
RMW Filter).

What it models: the RMW filter, the design under test; not the arbiter or the tag access checker.
The arbiter's output reaches it through the tag clear squash (both RTL), and `u_abvip_tags` plays
the tag access checker. The model drives no port; the properties compare its predictions with what
the RTL sends.

'''

==== Observed, modeled, checked

*Rule:* the model observes the four events on the RMW filter's ports, keeps the one operation in
flight, and predicts the RMW filter's three outputs, (3) to (5); the `rmw_*` and `contracts`
properties compare each prediction with what the RTL sends ([ToO] RMW Filter).

.The RMW model: what it observes, what it models, and how each output is checked
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig4["RMW model: observed, modeled, checked",align=center,width=900,height=711]

[cols="2,5,5,12,7",options="header"]
|===
|Point |Observed |Sent by |The model: what it keeps, or what it predicts |Checked by

|(1) |a request presented upstream, after the tag clear squash |RTL: the arbiter, from either
tag filter |keeps the operation: read or write, meta word, bit select `b`, tag `t`, `a_source`
|an input here; the arbiter checks cover it
|(2) |the downstream answer |testbench: `u_abvip_tags` |keeps the `Get` answer's word `W`, its
`d_error` and whether its response or data integrity is broken, then the write-back's answer
|an input
|(3) |the downstream request |RTL: the RMW filter |predicts the slot: the operation's `Get` of its
meta word, with its `a_source` (`REQ_RMW_01`, `REQ_RMW_03`); for a write whose bit differs and
whose `Get` had no error, one full-word `PutFullData` of `Upd(W, b, t)` (`REQ_RMW_06`,
`REQ_RMW_07`, `REQ_RMW_09`); nothing else (`REQ_RMW_04`, `REQ_RMW_13`, `REQ_RMW_16`). After a
faulty `Get` answer the write-back slot is open, whatever the bit, until the write is answered,
and nothing sent there is checked |`rmw_read`
A1; `rmw_write_skip` A1, A2; `rmw_write_back` A1, A2, A4; `rmw_single_op` A2; `rmw_errors` A1
|(4) |`a_ready` and the answer upstream |RTL: the RMW filter |predicts when a request may be
accepted: no operation unanswered, or the only one, a read, answered now (`REQ_RMW_10`,
`REQ_RMW_11`); the answer: `Bit(W, b)` for a read, `AccessAck` for an equal bit, the write-back's
answer otherwise, with `d_error` from the meta SRAM (`REQ_RMW_02`, `REQ_RMW_05`, `REQ_RMW_08`,
`REQ_RMW_14`), and `d_error` only then (`REQ_RMW_17`), none of it for a write after a faulty `Get`
answer; one answer per operation (`REQ_RMW_15`)
|`rmw_read` A2, A3; `rmw_write_skip` A3; `rmw_write_back` A3; `rmw_single_op` A1, A3, A4;
`rmw_errors` A2, A3
|(5) |the device and integrity faults to the alert logic |RTL: the RMW filter |keeps whether a meta
SRAM answer with `d_error`, or with a bad response or data integrity, was taken since reset;
predicts a fault only after one (contract C8) |`contracts` A8
|===

* The arbiter takes an answer with the `d_ready` of the input it returns to: the tag filter keeps
  it at 1 (`tf_flow` A1), and contract C3b keeps it at 1 for the engine in the liveness runs.
* The model observes the outputs (3) and (4) too: what the RMW filter has already sent decides
  what is due next (the `Get` taken, the write-back taken, the answer taken).

'''

==== One request, step by step

*Rule:* each event lands in the one operation, whatever the order the events come in; the checks
look in the cycle the RTL sends an output.

A capability store of tag 1 to `0x1000_1240`: its tag is bit 8 of the meta word `0x1100_8C48`,
which holds `0x0000_0080` (`rmw_write_back` C2), as in the figure:

[cols="1,6,4,5,6",options="header"]
|===
|Step |Event |Sent by |The model records |Checked here

|1 |the write presented upstream: tag 1, bit 8 of `0x1100_8C48` |RTL: the arbiter |a new
operation: write, `b` 8, `t` 1; it may be accepted now |-
|2 |the `Get` of `0x1100_8C48` downstream |RTL: the RMW filter |`WaitFill` |`rmw_write_skip` A1;
`rmw_write_back` A4; `rmw_single_op` A2
|3 |the write accepted upstream (`a_ready`), in the cycle its `Get` is taken |RTL: the RMW filter
|the operation is current |`rmw_single_op` A1, A2
|4 |the `Get` answer, `AccessAckData` `0x0000_0080` |testbench: `u_abvip_tags` |`W` =
`0x0000_0080`, `Filled`; `Bit(W, 8)` = 0, not 1: a write-back is due |an input
|5 |the write-back downstream, `PutFullData` `0x0000_0180` |RTL: the RMW filter |`WriteBackSent`
|`rmw_write_back` A1, A2, A4; `rmw_single_op` A2
|6 |the write-back's answer, `AccessAck` |testbench: `u_abvip_tags` |`WriteBackAcked`, `d_error` 0 |an
input
|7 |the answer upstream, `AccessAck`, `d_error` 0 |RTL: the RMW filter |nothing new: it predicts
the write-back's answer |`rmw_write_back` A3; `rmw_single_op` A3
|8 |the answer taken (`d_ready`) |RTL: the arbiter |`Idle` |-
|===

* Steps 1 to 3 may happen in one cycle: the request passes to the downstream port combinationally
  ([ToO] Timing).

'''

==== One operation

*Rule:* the model holds one operation from its acceptance to its answer taken; one state, `step_q`,
says how far it got, and each step says which downstream request may come next and which answer
is due ([ToO] RMW Filter).

[cols="3,6,6,3",options="header"]
|===
|Step |Downstream request allowed |Upstream |Spec

|`Idle` |the `Get` of the request presented upstream, taken only in the cycle that request is
accepted |a request may be accepted |[ToO] Timing; `REQ_RMW_10`, `REQ_RMW_16`
|`GetOwed` |its `Get`, once |nothing |`Passthrough`
|`WaitFill` |nothing |the answer may leave in the cycle the word `W` arrives |`Fill`
|`Filled` |for a write whose `Bit(W, b)` differs from `t` and whose `Get` had no error: its
write-back, `Upd(W, b, t)`; otherwise nothing |a read, an equal-bit write or an errored `Get` is
answered; a read answered lets the next request in, in the same cycle |`Fill`
|`WriteBackSent` |nothing |the answer may leave in the cycle the write-back's answer arrives
|`WriteBackReq`
|`WriteBackAcked` |nothing |the write-back's answer, with its `d_opcode` and `d_error`
|`WriteBackAck`
|===

* `op_q` holds the operation: read or write, meta word, `b`, `t`, `a_source`, then `W`, its
  `d_error` and its integrity. An answer counts in the cycle it arrives (one helper).
* No logic for an answer in the cycle of acceptance: the tag access checker answers in a later
  cycle (contract C10); if it did, `rmw_single_op` A3 would fail.

'''

The checker holds 472 flops of its own; the tag filter model's two entries, 200 bits, are the

top, the bind, the rule macro and the script are the one FPV environment's, shared with checker 2
([TB] One environment, one task per checker). Jasper elaborates the whole design once, so its
default task holds the real RTL. Checker 1 has three tasks, `task_TagPath_Main`,
`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` and `task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`, each with its checks and rules and
cut points on the blocks outside checker 1 (formal-verification skill, jasper-tcl.md, One task

[[uw_tf_forward]]
==== tf_forward: every access forwarded once

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_tf_forward[`tf_forward`]:
`REQ_TF_01a`, `REQ_TF_01b`, `REQ_TF_01c`, `REQ_TF_07`, `REQ_TF_16a`, `REQ_TF_16b`. In plain words:
the tag filter passes each core request to `xbar_main` once, unchanged and in the same cycle, and
passes the answer back with the xbar answer's fields as soon as its last part is in. Formula: every
core request `r` that is not an `NvmCapStore` appears once on `cored_tl_h` with every A-channel
field of `r`, in the first cycle `r` is presented; the answer to `r` carries the xbar answer's
`d_opcode`, `d_size`, `d_source`, `d_data` and data integrity (and its response integrity when no
meta error is merged in), in the cycle its last part arrives.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a request is presented on `cored_tl_d`, not yet forwarded, not a capability store to the NVM |a
request on `cored_tl_h` in the same cycle, every A-channel field equal |Main
|A2 |a request is presented on `cored_tl_h` |a core request presented and not yet forwarded |Main
|A3 |the tracked request's answer is presented |its xbar answer has arrived, and the answer's
`d_opcode`, `d_size`, `d_source`, `d_data`, data integrity equal it; the response integrity too
unless a meta error is merged |Main
|A4 |the head's last part has arrived; an answer is presented |the answer is presented then; and not
before |Main
|A5 |a core request is accepted |its xbar request is taken now, or was before |Main
|===

*Code:* the `tf_forward:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

|A2 |a meta request is presented and is no owed or possible tag write |a presented request with

|A2 |a lookup of a write is presented |its tag equals the core's tag sideband |Main
|A3 |a lookup is presented |it is a `Get` exactly when the core request is |Main

`d_error` |Main

[[uw_tf_flow]]
==== tf_flow: no stall, no lost answer

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_tf_flow[`tf_flow`]:
`REQ_TF_14`, `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`. In plain words: the meta port always takes its answers,
so the two tag filters sharing the RMW filter cannot deadlock, and every request is accepted and
answered once. Formula: the meta port's `d_ready` is 1 whenever a meta answer is offered; every

=== WTRC

*Rule:* a capability store to the NVM is checked at three points of the tag filter figure
(<<Tag filter>>): its `Get` on `cored_tl_h` (4), the absence of a lookup and the tag write on the
meta port (5), and its answer (6); and at a fourth, the WTRC fault to the alert (7), with the alert
request it raises (alert figure, <<checks_alerts>>). Each is checked against the tag
filter model's WTRC sequence and `Match` ([TP] WTRC).

[[uw_wtrc_store]]
==== wtrc_store: a capability store to the NVM reads, never writes

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_wtrc_store[`wtrc_store`]:
`REQ_WTRC_01`, `REQ_WTRC_02`, `REQ_WTRC_03`, `REQ_WTRC_05`, `REQ_WTRC_13`. In plain words: a
capability store to the NVM is not written: it reaches `xbar_main` as a `Get` of its word, makes no
lookup, and is answered `AccessAck`, untagged, by the WTRC. Formula: for an `NvmCapStore` word `r`,
`cored_tl_h` carries a `Get` of `r`{empty}'s word with a valid command integrity; W0 makes no meta
request and W1 none but its tag write; each word is answered once, `AccessAck`, untagged,
`d_source = a_source`, valid response integrity.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a capability store word is presented, not yet forwarded |a full-word `Get` of its word on
`cored_tl_h` in the same cycle |Main
|A2 |that `Get` is presented |a valid command integrity |Main
|A3 |a capability store word is presented |no meta request, or only an owed or possible tag write
|Main
|A4 |a capability store word's answer is presented |`AccessAck`, untagged, `d_source` its
`a_source`, valid response integrity |Main
|===

`REQ_WTRC_13` (every other access unchanged, with unchanged timing) has no property of its own: it
is the forwarding checks (`tf_forward` A1-A5) and the lookup checks (`tf_lookup` A1-A2), which run
with the WTRC in place.

*Code:* the `wtrc_store:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

[[uw_wtrc_compare]]
==== wtrc_compare: which stores set the tag

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_wtrc_compare[`wtrc_compare`]:
`REQ_WTRC_04a`, `REQ_WTRC_04b`, `REQ_WTRC_06`-`REQ_WTRC_09`. In plain words: each word is compared
with what the NVM holds; only when both words match does W1 turn into the capability's tag write,
ahead of any lookup; a mismatch fails the store with `d_error`, never with an alert. Formula:
`Match(w) = ReadOk(w) and FullPut(w) and InSeq(w) and Data(w) == NvmData(w) and DataIntg(w) ==
NvmDataIntg(w)`; W0's `d_error = not Match(W0)`; W1 issues one tag write of tag 1 to
`TagWord(c)`, `TagBit(c)` if both matched, after W1's NVM answer and before any later lookup; W1's
`d_error` is the tag write's error if issued, else 1.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |W0's answer is presented, with no fault and its NVM answer in |`d_error = not Match(W0)` |Main
|A2 |a meta request is presented while a tag write is owed |it is the tag write: a write, tag 1,
`TagWord(c)`, `TagBit(c)` |Main
|A3 |W1's answer is presented and its tag write was owed |the tag write's answer has arrived;
`d_error` is its error |Main
|A4 |W1's answer is presented, no fault, no tag write owed or possible |`d_error` |Main
|A5 |the WTRC's fault input is raised |a cause of `wtrc_faults` has occurred since reset |Main
|A6 |W0's or W1's answer is presented |its NVM answer has arrived, now or before |Main
|===

*Code:* the `wtrc_compare:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

[[uw_wtrc_faults]]
==== wtrc_faults: what the core cannot produce

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_wtrc_faults[`wtrc_faults`]:
`REQ_WTRC_10`, `REQ_WTRC_11`, `REQ_WTRC_12`. In plain words: a capability store word with a bad
integrity fails with `d_error`, sets no tag and raises the fatal alert. The spec says the same for a
word out of sequence or partial, and that any other request out of sequence raises the alert; those
need a core that breaks its access order, which is out of scope ([TP] Not covered by this
testplan), so only the integrity faults are reached. Formula: a capability store word out of sequence,
partial, with a bad command or data integrity, or with a bad NVM response integrity is answered
with `d_error`, writes no tag and raises `fatal_fault`; any other request out of sequence raises
`fatal_fault`.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a faulty word's answer is presented, its NVM answer in |`d_error`; no tag write is owed for it,
so the no-unneeded-lookup check (`tf_lookup` A2) fails on one |Main
|A2 |a faulty capability store word is seen |the alert request rises, at some point |Main
|===

*Code:* the `wtrc_faults:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

=== 2:1 tag arbiter

*Rule:* a request leaving the arbiter must be `Fwd(r, i)` of the request on input `i`, in the same
cycle; an answer from the RMW filter must reach input `s & 1`, with `s >> 1`, in the same cycle
([TP] 2:1 tag arbiter). A check about one input runs on each input `i`, in a loop: a free
choice of input would check only one input per simulation (simulation).

[cols="1,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Point |Compares |Checks

|(1) |the arbiter output with `Fwd(r, i)` of input `i`{empty}'s request; in `task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`, that
each input's request is accepted at some point |`arb_forward` A1, A2; `arb_flow` A1, A3
|(2) |the RMW filter's upstream request with the arbiter output, for input 0 |`arb_forward` A3
|(3) |the answer at input `s & 1` with the RMW filter's answer `s` |`arb_return`; `arb_flow` A2
|===

'''

.Flowcharts: each step with its rule, signals and asserts, then the same steps in SV (click to expand)
[%collapsible]
====
.One tag request through the 2:1 tag arbiter, step by step
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig7["one tag request through the 2:1 tag arbiter, step by step",align=center,width=870,height=1604]

====

'''

[[uw_arb_forward]]
==== arb_forward: each request forwarded once, with its sideband

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_arb_forward[`arb_forward`]:
`REQ_ARB_01`-`REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_ARB_11`. In plain words: the arbiter passes each tag request it
accepts to the RMW filter once, with its input number added at the bottom of `a_source` so that the
answer finds its way back; the core's request reaches the RMW filter as the arbiter sent it.
Formula: a request accepted on input `i` leaves the
arbiter once, as `Fwd(r, i)`; a request from input 0 reaches the RMW filter exactly as the arbiter
forwards it.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a request is accepted on input `i` |the output takes `Fwd(r, i)` in that cycle |Main
|A2 |a request is presented at the output |it is `Fwd(r, i)` of the request on input
`i = a_source & 1`, taken with it |Main
|A3 |the output presents a request from input 0 |the RMW filter's upstream request equals it |Main
|===

*Code:* the `arb_forward:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

[[uw_arb_return]]
==== arb_return: each answer to the input that asked

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_arb_return[`arb_return`]:
`REQ_ARB_05`, `REQ_ARB_06`, `REQ_ARB_07`. In plain words: each answer goes back only to the input
that asked, with the input number taken off `a_source` again and nothing else changed. Formula: an
answer with `d_source = s` goes to input `s & 1` only, with `d_source = s >> 1` and every other
D-channel field and the tag unchanged.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |an answer is presented at input `i` |the RMW filter presents an answer naming `i` |Main
|A2 |the RMW filter presents an answer `s` |input `s & 1` gets `d_source = s >> 1` |Main
|A3 |as A2 |every other D-channel field and the tag unchanged; `d_data` only in an
`AccessAckData`, the one answer that carries data ([TLUL]) |Main
|A4 |as A2 |the RMW filter's answer is taken exactly when its input takes it |Main
|===

With the forwarding check (`arb_forward` A1) and the TL-UL rule that a device answers with
`d_source = a_source`, the shifted-source check (A2) returns to each requester the `a_source` it
sent, whenever its bit 7 is 0.

*Code:* the `arb_return:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

[[uw_arb_flow]]
==== arb_flow: no added cycle, no starvation

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_arb_flow[`arb_flow`]:
`REQ_ARB_08`, `REQ_ARB_09`, `REQ_ARB_10`. In plain words: the arbiter adds no cycle in either
direction, and it never leaves one input waiting for ever. Formula: a request alone reaches the RMW
filter in the cycle it is presented, and an answer reaches its input in the cycle the RMW filter
gives it; a request held on either input is eventually accepted, given the RMW filter keeps
accepting.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |input `i` presents and the other does not |the output presents `Fwd(r, i)` in that cycle |Main
|A2 |the RMW filter presents an answer `s` |input `s & 1` presents it in that cycle |Main
|A3 |input `i` presents a request |it is accepted, at some point; the RMW filter keeps accepting
(contract C2, proven here) |EveryReqAnswered
|===

The testplan has no *Never* line for `arb_flow` yet; the rows below are the lines proposed for
it.

*Code:* the `arb_flow:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

=== RMW filter

*Rule:* each downstream request must be the `Get` or the write-back the RMW model has a slot for,
with the fields the spec gives; each upstream answer must carry `Bit(W, b)`, an `AccessAck`, or the
write-back's answer ([TP] RMW filter).

[cols="1,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Point |Compares |Checks

|(3a) |the downstream `Get` with the operation's word and `a_source` |`rmw_read` A1;
`rmw_write_skip` A1; `rmw_write_back` A4; `rmw_single_op` A1, A2
|(3b) |the write-back with `Upd(W, b, t)`, its opcode, size, word and integrity; its absence when the
bit is equal or the `Get` failed |`rmw_write_back` A1, A2, A4; `rmw_write_skip` A2; `rmw_errors` A1
|(4) |the upstream answer with `Bit(W, b)`, `AccessAck` or the write-back's answer, and its `d_error`
both ways |`rmw_read` A2; `rmw_write_skip` A3; `rmw_write_back` A3; `rmw_errors` A2, A3;
`rmw_single_op` A3
|===

'''

.Flowcharts: each step with its rule, signals and asserts, then the same steps in SV (click to expand)
[%collapsible]
====
.One RMW tag read, step by step
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig8["one RMW tag read, step by step",align=center,width=890,height=1423]

.One RMW tag write, step by step
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig9["one RMW tag write, step by step",align=center,width=890,height=1450]

====

'''

[[uw_rmw_read]]
==== rmw_read: a read returns its bit

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_rmw_read[`rmw_read`]:
`REQ_RMW_01`, `REQ_RMW_02`, `REQ_RMW_11`. In plain words: to read a tag, the RMW filter reads its
whole meta word once and returns the one bit; a read right after a read is not held up. Formula: a
read issues one `Get` of its meta word downstream; its answer's tag is `Bit(W, b)` (not checked with
`d_error`); a read presented in the cycle the previous read is answered is accepted then, if the
downstream port is ready.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a downstream request is presented in a read's `Get` slot |a `Get` of the read's word with its
`a_source` |Main
|A2 |a read's answer is presented upstream |its `Get` answer has arrived; without `d_error`, the tag
is `Bit(W, b)` |Main
|A3 |a read is presented as the previous read is answered, downstream ready |it is accepted in that
cycle |Main
|===

*Code:* the `rmw_read:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

[[uw_rmw_write_skip]]
==== rmw_write_skip: an equal bit is not written

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_rmw_write_skip[`rmw_write_skip`]:
`REQ_RMW_03`, `REQ_RMW_04`, `REQ_RMW_05`. In plain words: to write a tag, the RMW filter first
reads the meta word; if the bit already holds the tag, it writes nothing and only acknowledges.
Formula: a write first issues a full-word `Get` of its
meta word; if `Bit(W, b) == t` it issues no write-back and is answered `AccessAck`.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a downstream request is presented in a write's `Get` slot |a full-word `Get` (size 2, mask `4'hF`) of its word |Main
|A2 |a downstream request is presented |not while the current write's bit equals its tag |Main
|A3 |such a write's answer is presented |`AccessAck` |Main
|A4 |a write's answer is presented upstream |its `Get`{empty}'s answer has arrived, now or before |Main
|===

The no-write-back check (A2) and the `AccessAck` check (A3) claim nothing when the write's `Get`
answer is faulty (no `d_error`, a broken response or data integrity): the alert is raised and the
case is a don't-care (the decision to ignore a corrupted read in the RMW filter).

*Code:* the `rmw_write_skip:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

[[uw_rmw_write_back]]
==== rmw_write_back: a changed bit is written back alone

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_rmw_write_back[`rmw_write_back`]:
`REQ_RMW_06`-`REQ_RMW_09`. In plain words: if the bit differs, the RMW filter writes the whole
word back with only that bit changed, and passes the memory's answer to that write up as the
write's answer. Formula: if `Bit(W, b) != t`, the filter writes back `Upd(W, b, t)`
with one full-word `PutFullData` to the same meta word, with freshly computed command and data
integrity; the write-back's answer is forwarded as the write's answer; every downstream request of
the write carries its `a_source`.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |the write-back is presented |its data is `Upd(W, b, t)` |Main
|A2 |the write-back is presented |a full-word `PutFullData` to the same word, valid command and data
integrity |Main
|A3 |a write whose bit differs is answered upstream |its write-back's answer is presented
downstream in that cycle; same `d_opcode` and `d_error` |Main
|A4 |a write's `Get` or write-back is presented |the write's `a_source` |Main
|===

The write-back checks (A1-A3), and the source check (A4) for the write-back, claim nothing when the
write's `Get` answer is faulty: whether a write-back follows, what it carries (its `a_source` too)
and how the write is answered are don't-cares (the decision to ignore a corrupted read in the RMW
filter).

*Code:* the `rmw_write_back:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

[[uw_rmw_single_op]]
==== rmw_single_op: one operation at a time

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_rmw_single_op[`rmw_single_op`]:
`REQ_RMW_10`, `REQ_RMW_15`, `REQ_RMW_16`. In plain words: the RMW filter works on one tag access at
a time, answers each one once, and sends the meta SRAM nothing it was not asked for. Formula: a new
request is accepted only when no operation is unanswered, or in the cycle the only unanswered
operation, a read, is answered; every accepted request is answered once, given the meta SRAM
answers; the downstream port carries one `Get` per accepted request, plus one write-back for a write
whose bit changes, and nothing else.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a request is accepted upstream |the filter may take one now |Main
|A2 |a downstream request is presented; a `Get` for a presented request is taken |a slot is open;
the request is accepted in that cycle |Main
|A3 |an answer is presented upstream |an operation is unanswered |Main
|A4 |an operation is unanswered |its answer is taken upstream, at some point, given the meta SRAM
answers (contract C1) |EveryReqAnswered
|===

The downstream check's write-back slot (A2) is also open for a write whose `Get` answer is faulty,
whether or not its bit differs, until the write is answered: what the filter then sends for that
write is a don't-care (the decision to ignore a corrupted read in the RMW filter).

*Code:* the `rmw_single_op:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

[[uw_rmw_errors]]
==== rmw_errors: device errors

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_rmw_errors[`rmw_errors`]:
`REQ_RMW_13`, `REQ_RMW_14`, `REQ_RMW_17`. In plain words: when the meta SRAM reports an error, the
RMW filter writes nothing after it, and passes the error to the requester; it adds no error of its
own. Formula: a device error on the `Get`
of a write aborts it: no write-back; a device error on any meta SRAM answer reaches the requester as
`d_error`.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a downstream request is presented |not while the current write's `Get` answer had `d_error` |Main
|A2 |an answer is presented upstream, after a downstream answer with `d_error` |`d_error` |Main
|A3 |an answer is presented upstream with `d_error` |its `Get` answer or its write-back's answer
had `d_error` |Main
|===

The two error-passing checks (A2, A3) claim nothing for a write whose `Get` answer is faulty, even
when its write-back is answered with `d_error` (the decision to ignore a corrupted read in the RMW
filter).

*Code:* the `rmw_errors:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

'''

A8

|(7) |the tag filter's WTRC fault output with the WTRC causes since reset (tag filter model)
|`wtrc_compare` A5, which is also the WTRC part of `contracts` A8

(5) and (7) are numbered as in the RMW model's and the tag filter model's figures.

[[uw_tag_alerts]]
==== tag_alerts: the tag path's faults raise the alert

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_tag_alerts[`tag_alerts`]:
`REQ_TAG_07`, `REQ_TAG_08`, `REQ_TAG_10`. In plain words: an error or a broken integrity on a meta
SRAM answer to the tag path raises the fatal alert, which stays up until reset. Formula: a device
error on a meta SRAM answer to the tag path, or an integrity fault on one, requests `fatal_fault`;
once raised, the alert stays raised until reset (premise P2, the alert sender's own behaviour).

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |the RMW filter takes a meta SRAM answer with `d_error` |the alert request rises, at some point
|Main
|A2 |it takes one with a broken response or data integrity |the alert request rises, at some point
|Main
|===

`REQ_TAG_10` has no property here: it is premise P2.

*Code:* the `tag_alerts:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

[[uw_contracts]]
==== contracts: what checker 1 proves for the other checkers

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_contracts[`contracts`],
checks A2, A4, A6, A7, A8: contracts C2, C4, C6, C7 and C8, proven here and assumed in checkers 2
and 3 (TB architecture, Contracts).

[cols="2,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A2, contract C2 |a request is presented on the RMW filter's upstream port |it is accepted, at some
point |EveryReqAnswered
|A4, contract C4 |an answer is offered downstream |the RMW filter takes it, at some point |TagsRspTaken
|A6, contract C6 |an answer is presented on `cored_tl_d` |its `d_source` is the oldest unanswered
request's `a_source` |Main
|A7, contract C7 |a meta request waits |it stays, with its tag and bit select, until taken |Main
|A8, contract C8 |a fault input of the WTRC or the RMW filter is raised |one of its causes has
occurred since reset |Main
|===

* Contract C7 holds only if the core holds its requests (assumption A1).
* Contract C8 is proposed: checker 3 would assume it. In checker 3
  the RMW filter is a blackbox, so the causes it names are not visible there: an open decision asks how
  checker 3 uses it.

*Code:* the `contracts:` banner section of link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv`].

[[uw_tlul_protocol]]
==== tlul_protocol: every port follows TL-UL

*Implements:* xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#tp_tlul_protocol[`tlul_protocol`]
A1: the TL-UL rules on every port of the checker, assumed where the testbench drives and asserted
where the design drives.

[cols="1,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|A1 |a beat on a channel the design drives |it follows TL-UL |Main
|===

* Six ABVIP instances do it: the four of <<_environment>>, `u_abvip_core`, `u_abvip_xbar`,
  `u_abvip_m1`, `u_abvip_tags`, and the checker's two `CheckBoth` instances, `u_abvip_m0` and
  `u_abvip_rmw`. Their rules and covers are the ABVIP doc's ([ABVIP], TL01-TL13,
  `Req_Opcode` ... `Rsp_Param`): each rule is an `assert_` on the end the design drives, and on both
  ends in the two `CheckBoth` instances. This testpoint has no property of its own.
* Asserted, by port: the tag filter's answers on `cored_tl_d`; its requests on `cored_tl_h`; the
  arbiter's answers on input 1; the RMW filter's requests downstream; both channels of arbiter
  input 0 and of the RMW filter upstream.
* Expected failures, Suspected: `u_abvip_m1` TL11 (`Rsp_Opcode`), when the tag clear squash
  answers an engine's `Put` with `AccessAckData`; `u_abvip_rmw` TL07, when it turns a
  `PutPartialData` with a gapped mask into a `Get`. Triage each CEX against the spec before
  anything else (formal-verification skill, CEX triage).

'''
